newsitem.title: USA: Alco's Unisource Q4 revs off 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Alco's Unisource Q4 revs off 3 pct.

text.p: Alco Standard Corp said Wednesday its Unisource Worldwide Inc unit had fiscal fourth quarter revenues of $1.8 billion, down 3.0 percent from a year ago in an environment where average printing paper prices were 18 percent lower than a year earlier.
Net income in the quarter, ended September 30, was down 66.5 percent and totalled $11.1 million after $17 million in inventory valuation adjustments and bad-debt charges.
Earnings per share dropped to $0.08 from $0.28 a year earlier.
Alco anounced in the third quarter that it plans to spin ff Unisource by December 31.
It said Unisource's fiscal 1996 revenues were $7 billion, flat with 1995 despite decreased pricing for printing and imaging papers.

Net income was $60 million, reflecting a $50 million pre-tax charge against earnings taken in the third quarter for additional restructuring expenses. Excluding this special charge, net income from Unisource was $92 million, down 12 percent from last year.
"Our primary operating focus will be on growing revenues, managing assets and increasing cash flow," said Ray Mundt, chairman and chief executive officer of Unisource.
"We're in the process of creating a more balanced contribution from our printing and imaging and supply systems businesses," he said.

"Our supply systems acquisition strategy, as well as our segmented marketing programs, are designed to provide that balance," he continued. "As we realize our goal, we'll be able to provide more predictable, sustainable performance levels for our shareholders."
